- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (-1.00) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon — adjust upward by 2–5% for such spikes.  
- Model overestimates early 30-day lows — apply downward bias of 1–3% for the first 5–7 days of forecast.  
- Model shows mean reversion bias — if price is trending sharply up/down, forecast should lag slightly to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to positive within 3–5 days, model should adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to capture sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is neutral and price is trending, model should not overreact — keep forecast close to 3–5 day moving average.
